notes.meaning: John sees an angel come down from heaven holding a large chain and the key to the deep pit called the Abyss. God gives this angel full authority to lock up the powers of evil. Even the greatest demonic powers cannot resist God's command.

The angel grabs the dragon, who is Satan, and binds him for a thousand years. God gives Satan four names to show his cruelty, trickery, and hatred toward believers. The devil is completely helpless before God's messenger and cannot escape his appointed punishment.

differ.view: Believe Satan will be bound literally for a future thousand-year period when Christ returns to reign on earth.
Believe the thousand years is a symbol for the entire church age, during which Christ limits Satan's power so the gospel can reach the nations.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Teach that the thousand years represents the present age of the Christian church rather than a future earthly kingdom.

notes.meaning: The angel locks and seals Satan in the bottomless pit so he can no longer trick the nations of the world. His main weapon has always been lies and deception, but God takes that power away. God will allow him to be set free for a short time at the end of the period.

John sees thrones where faithful believers receive authority to reign. He notices especially the souls of martyrs who were put to death for following Jesus and refusing to worship the beast. These faithful followers come to life and share in Christ's royal rule for a thousand years.

differ.view: The Assemblies of God teaches a *premillennial* view (the belief that Jesus returns *before* the thousand years). It officially holds that Christ will visibly return to earth to establish a literal, earthly kingdom of peace and righteousness, where His saints will reign with Him for a thousand years before the final judgment.

The Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod officially rejects any future earthly kingdom, holding an *amillennial* view (the belief that the thousand years is a symbol, not an earthly government). In its official doctrinal statement, the synod teaches that the passage describes Christ's current spiritual rule in heaven, and that the church on earth remains under the cross until Christ returns once for the final judgment.

notes.meaning: The rest of the dead do not rise until the thousand years come to an end. The rising of God's faithful people to reign with Christ is called the first resurrection. This shows the special honor and life God gives to those who belong to Him.

differ.view: Believe the first resurrection is the physical raising of the righteous, while the unsaved dead remain in their graves until after the thousand years.
Believe the first resurrection is spiritual new birth from sin in this life, rather than a bodily resurrection.

notes.meaning: God blesses everyone who shares in this first resurrection, calling them holy. The second death, which means eternal separation from God, has no claim on them. Instead, they serve as priests to God and Christ, reigning with Him in perfect safety.

When the thousand years are finished, God allows Satan to come out of his prison for a final moment. He immediately returns to his old work of deceiving the nations from every corner of the earth, called Gog and Magog, gathering a massive army for war. This shows that the devil never changes his evil ways and that human hearts easily fall into rebellion without God's grace.

This vast enemy army marches across the earth and surrounds God's people and His beloved city. Yet no human battle ever takes place, because fire falls from heaven and destroys the attackers at once. God easily defends His church and wipes out those who fight against Him.

The devil who tricked mankind is thrown into the lake of burning sulfur to join the beast and the false prophet. This is his final end, not a temporary prison like the pit. There they will suffer unending punishment day and night forever.

John sees a great white throne and God sitting on it in perfect holiness and majesty. The old earth and sky vanish from His sight because they cannot endure His pure presence. No one can hide or run away from this final court.

All the dead, whether powerful or lowly in this life, stand before God to be judged. Books are opened that record everything people have done, alongside the Book of Life that contains the names of God's redeemed people. God examines every life with perfect fairness and complete knowledge.

differ.view: Believe this throne is only for the unsaved dead, since believers were already raised and rewarded before this point.
Believe all people, both believers and unbelievers, stand before this throne, where the works of believers publicly confirm their saving faith in Christ.

notes.meaning: The sea, Death, and the realm of the dead give up all who were in them so their bodies and souls can be reunited. No matter where or how a person died, no one is missed or forgotten. Every single individual is judged according to what they have done.

Death and the grave are thrown into the lake of fire, which means they are destroyed forever. This eternal punishment is called the second death. Christ's victory is so complete that dying will never touch His people again.

Anyone whose name is missing from the Book of Life is cast into the lake of fire. Good deeds alone cannot save a person apart from God's forgiveness through Christ. The only way to escape this terrible end is to belong to Jesus.
